text:
sasha: Heads-up — saw a weird accounting spike when a request fell back from dedicated-us-east to hosted-eu and then got truncated by the client. Console shows both provisional tokens (from the fallback path) and final charge, so customer saw double-ish units for one user. Anyone else?
jamie: Ugh. Repro steps?
sasha: Pretty simple: long streaming chat -> router fails to get capacity in us-east -> routes to hosted-eu as provisional session -> client network hiccup -> client sends cancel, then reconnect -> final session landed on hosted-eu but with truncated final token count. Console shows provisional + final.
ryan: Can you paste the router logs? suspect we didn't emit an accounting finalization event on fallback path.
sasha: snippet from router logs: ```INFO route decision: target=dedicated-us-east provisional_session=ps-9a1b route_id=rt-7f3``` 
```WARN fallback: route=dedicated-us-east -> hosted-eu reason=capacity threshold breach```
Then billing-bot event: ```PROVISIONAL_CREDIT session=ps-9a1b tokens=467 ledger_id=prov-44```
meera: billing-bot also emitted FINAL_CHARGE later: ```FINAL_CHARGE session=fs-3c2 tokens=460 ledger_id=final-44``` note different session IDs.
jamie: Different session IDs explains it. We create provisional sessions during routing but when final session lands we currently create a fresh session id. Need to link them so final replaces provisional instead of stacking.
sasha: Agreed. UX request: console should show "provisional reconciled" instead of two discrete charges if they map. Right now customers see two lines and get confused.
ryan: Two implementation options: 1) keep current events but add an explicit reconciliation event referencing prov-44 -> final-44 which billing applies as adjust(-prov)+apply(+final) in one atomic ledger op; or 2) reuse session id across route handoffs (pass the original session id along headers so final charge overwrites provisional).
meera: Option 2 is simplest for ledgers but risky: headers travel across boundaries and we might leak internal session ids to hosted tier. Also some infra components regenerate ids today.
jamie: Also, reusing ids breaks immutability assumptions in the billing pipeline — events are append-only and id collisions could complicate replay.
sasha: Option 1 preserves append-only model. We can emit a RECONCILE event linking ledger_ids. That requires UI + ledger changes to collapse lines.
ryan: We'll need telemetry flags though: emit reconciliation_cohort tags so we can query and verify no net overcharge before rollout.
meera: Technical sketch: add header `X-Accounting-Parent: prov-<id>` on routing fallback path. When finalizer emits FINAL_CHARGE, it can include `parent_ledger_id`. Billing pipeline consumes FINAL_CHARGE; if parent_ledger_id present then it emits RECONCILE(prov, final) marker.
jamie: Pseudocode for header: ```X-Accounting-Parent: prov-44``` and event example: ```{ type: "final_charge", session: "fs-3c2", tokens: 460, parent_ledger: "prov-44" }```
sasha: Also need UI UX: in Console traces, show a single combined line with a small chevron to expand prov vs final, and show reconciliation status (pending/confirmed).
meera: For telemetry, add metric: accounting.reconciliations.count and accounting.reconciliations.delta_tokens so we can alert if delta > threshold.
ryan: What about toolcalls? If a streaming toolcall triggered provisional too, we need toolcall invocation id propagated as well. Otherwise tool-run may be charged twice.
jamie: Good catch. We should extend schema: parent_ledger_id OR parent_invocation_id. Billing handler resolves both.
billing-bot: FYI: I can emit synthetic reconciliation events in staging if you want to test UI flow. :robot_face:
sasha: Yes please. Can we gate with feature flag? Start in staging, then opt-in orgs, then full rollout.
jamie: Plan: implement RECONCILE event + header passthrough in router (meera), billing pipeline changes to collapse ledgers (ryan), console UI collapse view (sasha + product), telemetry + feature flag (jamie). Rollout: staging -> opt-in -> global.
meera: I'll send a PR for router header passthrough and a short spec for the RECONCILE event shape.
ryan: I'll work on billing handler change and add tests to ensure net tokens equal final only.
sasha: Thanks. Also add an alert if reconciliation rate > 1% of sessions after rollout. Customers notice anything >0.5% often.
jamie: Noted. @deploy-bot can we get a staging run for the router change once PR lands?
deploy-bot: deploy queued for staging cluster: infra-2 in 15m. (will post status)
sasha: Awesome. Closing the loop: once we have reconciliation events in staging, billing-bot — emit a sample and we'll validate console collapse UX. :thumbsup:
